# THE MOVEUM YOKOHAMA by TOYOTA GROUP Reopens with New Exhibition Featuring Monet and Japanese Ukiyo-e


News ReleaseEvents


Download all images


Early bird ticket sales begin today ahead of the October 24, 2026, reopening of THE MOVEUM YOKOHAMA, featuring the new exhibition The Impressionist Artist Monet and Ukiyo-e: The Beauty of Japan That Captivated Monet.


Toyota City, Japan, September 24, 2026―Last December, the Toyota Group, inspired by Yokohama's history and the city's vision for a "City of Cultural and Artistic Creation," opened THE MOVEUM YOKOHAMA by TOYOTA GROUP ("THE MOVEUM YOKOHAMA")*1 at Yamashita Pier as a venue offering "MOVE" through both movement and emotion. Visitors enjoyed an immersive experience combining stunning visuals and music in a vast space.


With this reopening, THE MOVEUM YOKOHAMA will launch a new program, The Impressionist Artist Monet and Ukiyo-e: The Beauty of Japan That Captivated Monet


, on Saturday, October 24, 2026. This program focuses on the innovative artistic expressions created by ukiyo-e artists, including Katsushika Hokusai, and explores their influence on the Impressionist painter Claude Monet.


In addition, Toyota's e-Palette*2 will provide transportation from the Yamashita Pier entrance to the venue at Shed No. 4. Building on the mobility experience that was well received by many visitors last time, automated driving trials are also planned for this reopening.


In addition to immersive art exhibitions, THE MOVEUM YOKOHAMA will offer art activities and workshops, and introduce the Toyota Group's cultural activities. By creating a space for cultural exchange open to the local community, Toyota aims to broaden opportunities for cultural experiences and generate synergies throughout the Yokohama area.
The Toyota Group aims to go beyond simply providing transportation to deliver "MOVE" that touches people's hearts, thereby creating new opportunities for inspiration and learning through culture. We hope visitors will look forward to the new emotional "MOVE" experience that THE MOVEUM YOKOHAMA has to offer.


Please see the official website ([https://global.toyota/info/themoveum/](https://global.toyota/info/themoveum/) ) for more details and ticket information.


*1 "MOVEUM" is a neologism combining "MOVE" and "MUSEUM," meaning a museum that generates new "MOVE." The name "THE MOVEUM" reflects the hope that it will be a place where a variety of new "MOVE" is created for the mind, body, society, and the future.


*2 A battery electric vehicle developed by Toyota Motor Corporation for use in a range of mobility services.

### About the Program


## The Impressionist Artist Monet and Ukiyo-e: The Beauty of Japan That Captivated Monet


One of the key sources of inspiration that broadened the world of Monet's art was ukiyo-e prints from Japan. The unique compositions, views of nature, and aesthetics created by Hokusai, Hiroshige, Utamaro, and others offered Monet new perspectives in his ongoing exploration of changes in light and nature, enriching the breadth of expression in Impressionism. This exhibition allows visitors to experience art unbound, presenting the dialogue between Monet's works and Japanese art. It takes Impressionist paintings outside their frames to fill the entire space in a fusion of imagery, music, architecture, and sound. Rather than merely looking at the art, visitors can experience a new viewpoint born from the encounter between Japanese and European art as they wander through this world.

### Monet's dining room: the ukiyo-e space that entranced Monet


Monet lived in his house at Giverny from 1883 until the end of his life. The dining room, a space that grew to symbolize that house, was decorated with prints by Hokusai, Hiroshige, and Utamaro that Monet treasured. The venue showcases a space inspired by that room.


* Image is for illustrative purposes only


### Ukiyo-e Gallery: Monet, Ukiyo-e, and the spaces between


Japanese ukiyo-e entranced Monet. This exhibit focuses on the bold compositions and richness of expression found in ukiyo-e, as well as the skills of the craftsmen who created these works. Through ukiyo-e depicting the lifestyles and cultures of the people of Edo, visitors can discover the depth of Japanese art that so fascinated Western artists when they first encountered it.


### Learning events for families (scheduled)


Family-oriented workshops and study programs are planned with the goal of fostering children's creativity through encounters with art and culture. Opportunities to combine cultural experiences with learning will be provided.


## LISTEN. ―WHITE NIGHT


LISTEN.―a sound time capsule woven for the future―has spent the past 10 years traveling the world to explore musical cultures and capturing these treasures of "sound" on film. In WHITE NIGHT, the latest installment in the ONE MOMENT series―which blends immersive art with music―we embark on a journey through the sounds of the North, which hold the secrets to survival.


"Let's "Encounter the Earth". Sing, play music, dance, laugh, and cultivate a brighter tomorrow."


―LISTEN. producer Tomoko Yamaguchi


### Profile of Tomoko Yamaguchi, LISTEN. producer


Tomoko Yamaguchi launched LISTEN., a 10-year project to explore music cultures around the world and compile them into a video library, in 2010. She has since produced short films and feature-length films. ([https://www.the-listen-project.com](https://www.the-listen-project.com/) )
In 2025, she held a LISTEN. exhibition at the "HOUSE OF MUSIC HUNGARY" in Budapest.
She published the book LISTEN. (Ikinobiru Books), which allows readers to "experience" music videos by scanning QR codes.
On her YouTube channel, Tomoko Yamaguchi KazeAna!?, she is currently sharing her journey of rediscovering the world. ([https://www.youtube.com/@tomoko_yamaguchi](https://www.youtube.com/@tomoko_yamaguchi) )


### Special exhibition and video of winners of the Toyota Dream Car Art Contest


THE MOVEUM YOKOHAMA is exhibiting winning works from the 19th Japan Contest of the Toyota Dream Car Art Contest. Visitors can see dream-filled works created from the free-spirited imaginations of children. At STUDIO, a special video is screened in which these award-winning works come to life as immersive imagery. We hope visitors will enjoy the worlds where children's imaginations soar.


About the Toyota Dream Car Art Contest
With "Your Dream Car" as its theme, this art contest, held by Toyota Motor Corporation, invites children to use their imaginations to create their visions of future mobility.
[https://www.toyota-dreamcarart.com/](https://www.toyota-dreamcarart.com/)
